## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

## Importing saved summary files
```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)

clean_data <- readRDS(here("data", "clean_data.rds"))
summary_table <- readRDS(here("data", "summary_table.rds"))
monthly_summary <- readRDS(here("data", "monthly_summary.rds"))
```

## Occurrence records by region
```{r occurrence}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(summary_table, aes(x = region, y = n_records, fill = region)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Whale Shark Occurrence: Ningaloo Reef vs Great Barrier Reef",
    x = NULL, y = "Number of records",
    caption = "Source: OBIS (obis.org), accessed via robis"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Seasonal patterns by region
```{r}
ggplot(monthly_summary, aes(x = month, y = n, fill = region)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Seasonal Whale Shark Occurrence Pattern by Site",
    x = "Month", y = "Number of records", fill = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Refining plots
```{r refining occurrence}
# Add best color choices that are easy to read for everyone and add context directly to plot so people don't have to flip between the plot and table to interpret
ggplot(summary_table, aes(x = region, y = n_records, fill = region)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = n_records), vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(title = "Whale Shark Occurrence: Ningaloo Reef vs Great Barrier Reef", x = NULL, y = "Number of Records") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
scale_fill_manual(values = c("Ningaloo Reef" = "#0072B2", "Great Barrier Reef" = "#D55E00"))
```

### Mapping actual occurrence points
```{r refining region}
# Mapping points to see occurence by region in a clear visual way
library(sf)
#install.packages("rnaturalearth")
library(rnaturalearth)
#install.packages("rnaturalearthdata")
library(rnaturalearthdata)

aus <- ne_countries(country = "Australia", scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# convert your clean data to sf points
points_sf <- st_as_sf(clean_data, coords = c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude"), crs = 4326)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = aus, fill = "grey95", color = "grey60") +
  geom_sf(data = points_sf, aes(color = region), alpha = 0.6, size = 1.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Ningaloo Reef" = "#0072B2", "Great Barrier Reef" = "#D55E00")) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(105, 160), ylim = c(-30, -8)) +
  labs(title = "Whale Shark Occurrence Records", color = "Region") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())



# Side-by-side comparisons for seasonal pattern
ggplot(monthly_summary, aes(x = month, y = n, fill = region)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~region, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Ningaloo Reef" = "#0072B2", "Great Barrier Reef" = "#D55E00")) +
  labs(title = "Seasonal Whale Shark Occurrence by Site", x = NULL, y = "Records") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13))




# Overlaid line/area chart
ggplot(monthly_summary, aes(x = month, y = n, color = region, group = region)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.3) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Ningaloo Reef" = "#0072B2", "Great Barrier Reef" = "#D55E00")) +
  labs(title = "Seasonal Occurrence Pattern: Ningaloo vs GBR", x = NULL, y = "Records", color = "Region") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

```
